fig1.title: Per-Section Pearson Correlations with Shuffled Baseline
fig1.caption: Observed Pearson correlations (blue) between Zipf-Mandelbrot curvature drift and semantic drift across 10 sections of Pride and Prejudice, compared to the mean of 10 shuffled-text baselines per section (orange). All observed values fall within the baseline distribution; no section reaches conventional significance.

fig2.title: Zipf-Mandelbrot Parameter Means Across Sections
fig2.caption: Mean exponent (s), curvature (b), and R² values for the Zipf-Mandelbrot fit across the first three sections (representative of all 10). Error bars show standard deviations across windows within each section. The exponent centers near 0.75, curvature shows high variability, and R² exceeds 0.96 indicating good fits.

fig3.title: Z-scores of Observed Correlations Against Shuffled Baseline
fig3.caption: Z-scores of observed Pearson correlations relative to the shuffled baseline distribution per section. All z-scores fall within ±1.5, confirming no section shows a statistically significant deviation from the null hypothesis of no correlation between curvature drift and semantic drift.
